assist.description: Assist, wired (pack assist, 0.31): the LLM behind the doorman, the ceiling it lives on, what Assist sees, the pipeline

llm.description: the house's LLM, through Home Assistant's own `ollama` integration: a config entry at `url`, a conversation agent on `model` with the Assist API

url.description: the LLM server's door (an address, never a host name the house does not resolve)

model.description: the model the agent runs — it must ALREADY be on the server: apply refuses to let Home Assistant download gigabytes through the brain

instructions.description: one line appended to Home Assistant's own prompt (default: the labels' — full sentences in the house's language, colours by their English name in tool calls)

history.description: how many turns the agent remembers in a conversation

think.description: let a thinking model think before answering (slower; off for a house)

ceiling.description: the LLM lives on a host that sleeps: a watchman says whether it is up and takes the knock (Le Veilleur's contract: GET /api/targets/<t> answers `up`, POST …/wake with a bearer raises it)

target.description: the target the LLM's host is, in the watchman's words

token.description: the NAME of the secret holding the watchman's client token (the value never enters this file); the brain reads it as `<name>_bearer`

every.description: seconds between two reads of the watchman

replies.description: the doorman's lines, in the house's language (defaults: the labels')

waking.description: the host sleeps: the knock is sent, this is said

unknown.description: the watchman cannot be read and the LLM did not answer

absent.description: the host is up and the LLM did not answer

no_agent.description: no LLM agent exists in the brain yet

expose.description: what Assist sees, beyond Home Assistant's own defaults

lights.description: roles = each room's lights and its role groups (« Le QG — Plafond »), never a single bulb; rooms = the rooms' lights alone; all = every bulb too

scenes.description: the rooms' looks as their scripts, under their labels (« Cinéma »)

also.description: entity ids to expose on top

never.description: entity ids to keep out (the permit-join switch of a coordinator is out by the product's own rule)

pipeline.description: the Assist pipeline the house speaks through (the preferred one)

prefer_local.description: the sentences answer first; the doorman sees only what they cannot — the one sanctioned floor-to-ceiling fallthrough

voice.description: the house's ears and mouth: Wyoming speech servers by their ADDRESS (a capability is an address, never a place); the pipeline speaks through them and the phone's mic appears. Either ONE door for both verbs (0.37 — a server announcing speech to text AND text to speech, such as the bridge wyoming_openai in front of a standard OpenAI-shaped speech server) or two doors (0.34). Both verbs or neither: ears without a mouth answer in silence

oneOf.description: one door, both verbs (0.37): the wyoming entry it makes carries the stt and the tts entity

url.description: tcp://<host>:<port> — the server's own --uri shape, an address the house resolves

voice.description: the voice's name as the server announces it (Piper: fr_FR-siwis-medium); default: the server's first voice for the house's language

oneOf.description: two doors (0.34): one Wyoming server per verb

stt.description: speech to text — a Wyoming server's door

url.description: tcp://<host>:<port> — the server's own --uri shape, an address the house resolves

tts.description: text to speech — a Wyoming server's door, and the voice it speaks with

voice.description: the voice's name as the server announces it (Piper: fr_FR-siwis-medium); default: the server's first voice for the house's language

mics.description: what asks, and from which room when it does not say one (0.34): a device of the brain's registry (the phone's companion app today, a satellite tomorrow) placed in its room — the local sentences take the room from the device

device.description: the device's name in the brain's registry (its own, or the one a person gave it)

room.description: the room it asks from unless it names one — an area id of the house
